MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 14, 2020

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:04 p.m., on January 14, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 9, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation to Former Mayor Raths

City Council Minutes  1  January 14, 2020
   Mayor Goodell presented former Mayor Raths with a gavel plaque.

P2. Opening Remarks by Mayor Goodell

  Mayor Goodell presented his introductory remarks.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated November 29, 2019 in the Amount of $534,164.29

6.  Check Register Dated December 20, 2019 in the Amount of $2,781,455.91

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  2  January 14, 2020
 8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s

  Received and filed.

  Received and filed.

11. Review and Approval of Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 20-21 A-B
  Annual Fiscal Period of July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021

  (1) Adopted Successor Agency Resolution 20-01 Approving the Recognized Obligation

  Subject to Submittal to and Review by the Orange Countywide Oversight Board and by the

  Approved the updated Sports Field Use and Allocation Policy as recommended by the

15. Second Amendment to Agreement with Matrix Imaging for Document Scanning
  Services

  Approved Second Amendment to Agreement with Matrix Imaging for an additional $50,000
  resulting in a total not-to-exceed amount of $100,000 for Document Scanning Services.

16. Safety Lighting LED Conversion-San Diego Gas & Electric Territory (CIP 16228)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with

City Council Minutes  3  January 14, 2020
   the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

12. City Sidewalk Speed Limit

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Ratty answered various questions
  from the City Council.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to adopt
  Ordinance 19-334 Amending Mission Viejo Municipal Code of Ordinances Section
  12.15.100 to Increase the Bicycle Speed on Sidewalks From 5 Miles Per Hour to 12 Miles
  Per Hour.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

13. Senior Mobility Program Expanded Service

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley pulled the report to highlight the benefits of this program. She
  announced that she spearheaded this program in 2003 and thanked former Director of
  Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle and current staff member Leslie McDonald
  for all their efforts in starting this program. She also thanked current staff members Mark
  Nix, Barbara Cassidy and Drew Fine for their continued efforts in managing the senior
  mobility program.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, approve
  California Yellow Cab agreement for expanded services with the Senior Mobility Program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARING

17. Zone Change ZC2019-22, Conditional Use Permit CUP2019-408, Planned Development
  Permit PDP2019-309, and Variance VAR2019-53, being petitions submitted by
  Confluent Development, doing business as CDP-MS Marguerite LLC, to permit
  development of an assisted living facility located at 28570 Marguerite Parkway, in the
  CH (Commercial Highway) zone. The 3-story, 166,000-square-foot facility would have
  132 living units with 166 beds, including 102 assisted living units with 136 beds, and 30
  memory/congregate care units with 30 beds. Below-grade parking is proposed with 121
City Council Minutes  4  January 14, 2020
   parking spaces, plus four surface spaces for a total of 125 parking spaces. Zone Change
  ZC2019-22 proposes a Senior Housing Overlay required to permit the senior/assisted
  living project

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Associate Planner Nick Lagura detailed the proposed project and shared images of the site
  plan.

  Mayor Goodell opened the public hearing at 6:25 p.m

  Matt Turner, Morning Star: Addressed the City Council on the company principals and the
  high-quality option for aging residents that this project will provide.

  H. McNeish, Confluent Development: Outlined the Morning Star assisted living facility
  project. He asked that Condition #84 (affordable housing in-lieu fee of $1.12 million) be
  removed and that Condition #85 (park in-lieu fee of $1.075 million) be approved by the
  Council.

  Mayor Goodell read written comments from the following current tenants who asked to be
  reimbursed for moving expenses: Chris Brown; Majid Tarkeshian; and Amir Badieozzaman.

  Richard Tindall, San Marino: Announced that his family is the owner of Avery Plaza and he
  asked that the Council approve the project.

  Patty O’Connor, M.V.: Spoke on behalf of the Cordova Home Owners Association in favor
  of the project and expressed that senior living facilities are needed within the City.

  Mike Conatser, San Clemente: Spoke against the project, stating that he didn’t feel it was a
  good location for this development and would be a burden to the current tenants.

  Mayor Goodell closed the public hearing at 7:18 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to strike
  Condition #84, that prior to issuance of a building permit or grading permit, the
  applicant/owner shall pay an affordable housing in-lieu fee of $1.12 million based on
  provisions of low and very low housing units for a period of 10 years.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  Kelley
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  introduce Ordinance 20-335 Approving Zone Change ZC2019-22”, Being a Petition
  Submitted by Confluent Development to Place a Senior Housing Overlay on 2.92 Acres of
  Property in the CH (Commercial Highway) Zone, Located at 28570 Marguerite Parkway,

City Council Minutes  5  January 14, 2020
   Further Described as Assessor Parcel Number 740-012-21; (2) adopt Resolution 20-01
  Approving Conditional Use Permit CUP2019-408, Planned Development Permit PDP2019-
  309, and Variance VAR2019-53 and adopting the Initial Study/Mitigated Negative
  Declaration Prepared for the Project; and (3) amend Condition #85 to reflect that prior to
  issuance of a building or grading permit (whichever occurs first), the applicant/owner shall
  pay a park in-lieu fee of $1.075 million in accordance with the City’s Local Park Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  Kelley
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18. City Council Committee and Regional Board/Committee Representative Appointments
  and Update Posting of FPPC Form 806 Online

  Mayor Goodell appointed Ed Sachs to serve on the Orange County Fire Authority Board of
  Directors.

  Motion made by Mayor Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
  appointment of Ed Sachs to represent Mission Viejo on the Orange County Fire Authority
  Board of Directors.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Goodell appointed Trish Kelley to serve as representative and himself to serve as
  alternate on the Transportation Corridor Agencies Board of Directors.

  Motion made by Mayor Goodell, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
  appointment of Trish Kelley as representative and Brian Goodell as alternate on the
  Transportation Corridor Agencies Board of Directors.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Goodell appointed Bob Ruesch to serve as representative on the Orange County
  Vector Control Board.

  Motion made by Mayor Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
  appointment of Bob Ruesch to serve as representative on the Orange County Vector Control
  Board.

City Council Minutes  6  January 14, 2020
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum congratulated Mayor Goodell and pointed out that Mission Viejo may
be the first City to have an Olympic gold medalist Mayor. She asked that staff publicize the
changes to the Sports Field Use and Allocation Policy that was on the Consent Calendar this
evening. Council Member Bucknum invited residents to “Connect SoCal” at Laguna Niguel City
Hall on January 21, from 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. The program will provide an overview of Southern
California Association of Governments (SCAG) Draft Program Environmental Impact Report
(PEIR) and collect public comments. She announced that she will be attending a ribbon cutting at
UFC Gym tomorrow at 4:00 p.m. and lastly, Council Member Bucknum mentioned that the
Chamber of Commerce is having a mixer at the Leonard Cancer Institute and residents are invited.

City Council Minutes  7  January 14, 2020
 Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths congratulated Mayor Goodell. He also thanked Fire and Police Services
for for their work during the holiday season.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs congratulated Mayor Goodell. He complimented the City’s holiday
decorations and thanked staff and the contractors for their work. He also reminded residents that
the City Council is elected to make tough decisions on behalf the residents and although there was
a spirited conversation earlier in the meeting, all of the Council Members have the City’s best
interests in their hearts. Council Member Sachs announced that on February 7 the Orange County
Fire Authority is holding its Best and Bravest Awards Ceremony and it is open to the public.
Finally, Council Member Sachs cautioned residents to stop running red lights.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked Council Member Sachs for his comments and concurred that the
Council can disagree on topics and still have respect for each other. She also voiced concern over
the red-light runners and encouraged residents to pay closer attention and take responsibility.
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she received many compliments on the City’s Christmas
decorations and thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee and staff for their efforts. She
noted that at the last Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) meeting she was elected Chair of the
San Joaquin Hills TCA. Council Member Kelley thanked Council Member Raths for his year of
service as Mayor in 2019 and congratulated Mayor Goodell for his upcoming year as Mayor.
Lastly, she reminded residents that the Character Word of the month of January is perseverance
and she mentioned that the Character Committee is looking for pictures that depict the monthly
character words.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell thanked his colleagues for their support and for trusting him with the leadership of
this great City Council. He announced that he had a wonderful holiday and two new
granddaughters were born in December. Mayor Goodell stated that he feels very blessed to serve
this community.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:31 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting in memory of Bob Reinicke to Tuesday, January 28, 2020,
at 5:00 p.m.

Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 28, 2020

City Council Minutes  8  January 14, 2020
